sections.h2: Where is the Greene County Recorder and when can you record a deed?
sections.html:
The Greene County Recorder's Office is on the third floor at 69 Greene St. in Xenia. Business hours run Monday through Friday from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the county lists recording hours of 7:30 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. on the recorder's page. A deed that arrives after the 3:00 cutoff may wait for the next business day.

The office keeps the permanent record of land transactions in the county. Its public list of filings is long, and a seller will meet several of these during a sale:

  • Deeds, mortgages and releases of mortgage
  • Easements, leases and land contracts
  • Affidavits, trusts and powers of attorney
  • Mechanic's liens, federal tax liens and child support liens
  • Plats, condominium documents and annexations

Military discharges are filed and certified here too, and they are not public record. The veteran or heirs can request them at no cost.

sections.h2: What must be done before the Greene County Recorder accepts a deed?
sections.html:
The deed goes through the Greene County Auditor first. The auditor's transfer page asks for a completed Statement of Value (DTE 100) or its exempt form (DTE 100 EX), the right fees payable to the auditor, a grantor name that reads the same way the grantor took title, and initials from the map department. Ohio deeds must be signed by the grantor and notarized.

Ohio law lists who may take the acknowledgment: a judge or clerk of a court of record, a county auditor, a county engineer, a notary public or a mayor, under R.C. 5301.01. Recording also protects the buyer. Under R.C. 5301.25 an unrecorded deed is treated as fraudulent against a later good-faith purchaser who had no knowledge of it.

If the land is in the CAUV farm program, or was the year before, a conveyance statement for that program must travel with the deed. Where a survey was made, the surveyor's name must appear in the deed.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Greene County?
sections.html:
Ohio sets recording fees in R.C. 317.32. Each fee splits into a base amount for the county and an equal amount for the housing trust fund. Senate Bill 94 allowed counties to add up to $5.00 to recording fees, and the Greene County Recorder announced on January 2, 2026 that standard document fees would not rise.

Recording fees printed in R.C. 317.32 (base plus housing trust fund)
ItemBase feeHousing trust fund fee
Record and index, first two pages$17$17
Each added page$4$4
Marginal reference by separate instrument$2$2
Certified copy, per page$1$1
Document preservation surchargeUp to $5None listed

Copies cost less when you make them. The county charges $.10 per page for self-service official copies, and $2.00 per page when staff make them.

sections.h2: What transfer charges apply before recording in Greene County?
sections.html:
The auditor collects those charges, not the recorder. The Greene County auditor's page prints a conveyance fee of $2.00 per thousand dollars of purchase price, made up of a $1.00 fee and a $1.00 transfer amount, and a $0.50 per parcel charge. The county posts a conveyance fee calculator online.

The grantor pays, per R.C. 322.02, and a county may levy no more than 30 cents per hundred dollars of value as its transfer tax. Statute lists transfers with no fee, and a few that matter to families are listed here:

  • Transfers among heirs or devisees of one decedent when no money changes hands
  • Gifts between spouses, or between a parent and child
  • Transfers into a revocable trust and back to the grantor
  • Deeds given only to secure or release a debt

The exemption reason is written on the statement, so check the box with the closing agent.

sections.h2: Which deed types does the Greene County Recorder file for a sale?
sections.html:
The state fee table covers the common choices, and each one is recorded at the same per-page rates: warranty deed, limited warranty deed, quit claim deed and survivorship deed. Estate sales add the executor's deed, administrator's deed, guardian's deed or trustee's deed, depending on who holds authority. A transfer on death designation affidavit is also on the list.

A survivorship deed follows R.C. 5302.20, where a clear intent in the deed creates a survivorship tenancy, and a conveyance by all tenants ends it. A seller who inherited with siblings should confirm in the record whether title sits in survivorship or in common before listing.

sections.h2: Which towns send deeds to the Greene County Recorder?
sections.html:
Ohio records a deed in the county where the land lies, so every parcel in the county's cities, villages and townships goes through the Xenia office. The cities are Beavercreek, Bellbrook, Fairborn and Xenia, and Kettering reaches into Greene County even though most of it lies in Montgomery County. Greene County was named for Revolutionary War General Nathanael Greene and borders Clark, Madison, Fayette, Clinton, Warren and Montgomery counties.

Roads run through the county on I-675, I-71, US 35, US 42 and US 68, which puts Beavercreek and Fairborn within reach of Dayton. The auditor's real estate department tracks more than 73,000 parcels, and each of those parcels has its own chain of recorded documents. A buyer's title search reads that chain back through earlier deeds, so a gap in the records can slow a sale.

Public school districts in the county are Beavercreek, Bellbrook-Sugarcreek, Cedar Cliff, Fairborn, Greeneview, Xenia Community and Yellow Springs.

sections.h2: How do you check records and get a mortgage release in Greene County?
sections.html:
The online Recorder's Document Search indexes documents from 1984 forward. Images posted online carry a watermark, and watermarked pages will not be accepted for recording, so get clean pages from the office. A property transfer tracking table shows the status of a recently submitted transfer, and a property fraud alert service sends a notice when a document is filed against a registered property.

After payoff, the lender has 90 days to file a release or satisfaction of mortgage. A seller who paid off a loan years ago should search the index for that release before listing, because a missing release can hold up a closing.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Greene County homes?
sections.html: The Census Bureau counts 68,166 households in Greene County for 2020 to 2024, with 2.38 people per household and about 74,000 housing units as of 2025. Median selected owner costs are $1,702 with a mortgage and $700 without. The county issued 567 building permits in 2025, and 92.8 percent of households have a broadband subscription, which helps with online document submissions.

faqs.q: What hours does the Greene County Recorder record documents?
faqs.a: The county lists recording hours of 7:30 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, with office business hours running until 4:00 p.m. Submit early in the day if you need same-day recording.

faqs.q: Does Greene County charge extra for recording after the state fee change?
faqs.a: No for standard documents. The recorder announced on January 2, 2026 that fees would stay where they were even though state law allows up to $5.00 more.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee on a Greene County deed?
faqs.a: The grantor pays it to the county auditor before the deed is presented to the recorder. The auditor's page prints the rate as $2.00 per thousand dollars of price, plus $0.50 per parcel.

faqs.q: How can I get a copy of my deed in Greene County?
faqs.a: Visit the recorder at 69 Greene St., third floor, or use the online document search. Self-service official copies are $.10 per page, and staff-made copies are $2.00 per page.

faqs.q: How long does a lender have to release a paid mortgage in Greene County?
faqs.a: Ninety days from payoff. The release is filed with the recorder, and copies can be requested at the office or found through the document search.
